anya: Postmortem follow-up: recurring overnight model-load spikes causing short 503 windows. We need a tiny runbook + triage script and clear owners. Target: ship within 2 weeks.

anya: Proposed split:
- Compact runbook (prescriptive 0/2/10m escalation). owner: ben. due: 2024-12-07
- `triage-lite.sh` (health, p50/p95, logs grab). owner: lee. due: 2024-12-07
- CronJob warmup at 23:50. owner: eng-platform. due: 2024-12-10
- Fallback routing to standby model variant. owner: anya. due: 2024-12-15

ben: Ill take the runbook. Will keep top of doc one-page checklist with exact commands and escalation phone matrix. Will create `docs/playbooks/short-model-load.md`.

lee: I'll own the script. Sketch below for `triage-lite.sh` (no tokens hardcoded):
```sh
# quick health
curl -fsS https://api.redwood-infer/health || echo "health failed"
# metrics p50/p95 (reads METRICS_KEY from env or secrets)
curl -sS "https://metrics/api?query=model_load_latency_p50" -H "Authorization: Bearer $METRICS_KEY" | jq .
curl -sS "https://metrics/api?query=model_load_latency_p95" -H "Authorization: Bearer $METRICS_KEY" | jq .
# logs (last 200 lines)
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=runtime --tail=200
```

anya: Good. Add a `--dry-run` flag and `--quick` mode to keep on-call friction low. Note in runbook: do not hardcode secrets.

anya: I'll gate playbook review until the script and cronjob PRs are linked. After PRs land, run a tabletop with on-call to validate ergonomics. Keep playbook prescriptive and minimal at the top.
